ui.title: Galaxy Genome Map
ui.calcCliff: Over the game's 150 ly ceiling, so it drops to 30. This drive needs {t} t or more to beat it.
ui.hCalcMass: Jump range uses your loaded mass, including cargo. Shield strength uses the hull's own base mass and ignores what you carry.
ui.hScannerBoost: An engineer can add 5-15% to a scanner's range. The map reads the fitted grade exactly, so a boosted ship reaches a little further than anything here says.
ui.hNoScan: Everything in the system, once you have flown to all of it. A system the game already counts as explored is worth nothing, so any threshold leaves those out on its own.
ui.arenaMods: Not available while a mod is active.
ui.pArenaWhat: 83 fixed battles at nine anarchy systems near Sol, the same opponents every game.
ui.hMatNote: A landable planet yields three materials, fixed for good. Matches are systems with a planet that yields this one.
ui.repNote: Distance from the main star, where a jump drops you. Nearest to Sol first.
ui.huntWarn: {n} of {total} classes have fewer systems than the task asks for.
ui.hGateBack: The Core-systems end of the warp gate that reaches {far}. Repair both ends and the trip is one jump either way.
ui.gateOther: The other end of the warp gate
ui.hVoidWhat: A cluster of 21 systems and 35 stations, 4,562 ly out and nowhere near anything else. Stations, outfitters and missions, in the middle of empty space.
ui.hSagWhat: The black hole at the centre of the galaxy, 25,899 ly out. Arriving once unlocks the Warp Drive Booster at every outfitter, for ever.
ui.hPreonWhat: The only Preon star in the galaxy, and the most valuable single discovery in the game at 13,020,000 CR. The generator never makes another.
ui.hIsarWhat: The Distant Colony, 21,981 ly out, and a warp gate from Wolf 1462 reaches it in one jump once both ends are repaired.
ui.hTermWhat: Foundation, 24,059 ly out, and the far end of the warp gate at PPM 41187: the deepest place a gate will take you.
ui.hValue: What the system banks for turning up, with the scanner you have fitted. Tick the box to add the one body worth crossing the system for.
ui.gatesNote: Every gate starts broken. Tick the ends you have repaired: routes use a gate only once both its ends are.
ui.pHighValueWhat: Every system banking 500,000 CR or more for turning up with a 1D fitted, generated space included.
ui.pOutfitWhat: HiTech stations, which are the only ones that sell the best modules at the best grades.
ui.pBlackWhat: The eight stations ever dealt Slaves or Tretonin, marked with the half of the turnover each one holds them in.
ui.pEngWhat: The five engineers, who upgrade modules past what any shop sells.
ui.pGatesWhat: The three warp gates: one jump each once both ends are repaired, and the only way to cross the galaxy quickly.
ui.pStationMeaning: An abandoned station waits in one of these five, and repairing it makes it your own base.
ui.pStationFive: Which one is decided when your save is created: LHS 3182 30%, 212 Puppis, HR 244 and GD 219 20% each, Wolf 1462 10%. Nothing marks it until you arrive.
ui.presetNote: Counts are the 5,340 catalogued systems. Generated space holds far more of everything except stations, engineers and gates, which it never holds at all.
ui.hSellsBlack: Only an Anarchy station ever stocks Slaves or Tretonin, and only these eight are ever dealt them. Which half is holding them flips every 4,000 units of goods you move; Olymp City is dealt them whatever the count.
ui.hBuysBlack: Medium, High and Conflict Zone security will take contraband off you, always at the premium price. Low security and Anarchy will not, so you cannot sell it back where you bought it.
ui.hOreBuyer: Mining Platform buys every mineral at the top demand tier, not just its first line. It is the one guaranteed best price for ore in the game, and no station sells minerals at all, so mining is their only source.
ui.hTrophyBuyer: Angler Eye, Angler Fang, Zentarks Stone and the Automaton Component sell nowhere else. Keep one Zentarks Stone: repairing a warp gate needs it.
ui.hNoMarket: Four stations have their market removed outright. They still repair and refuel, and the market screen is empty.
ui.hScannerNote: A star is discovered the moment you arrive, at any distance. A planet only pays once you come within the scanner's range of it, and the innermost orbit is 65 light seconds out.
ui.hArrivalNote: What the system banks the moment you drop out of warp. Everything else needs flying to, one body at a time.
ui.hHopsNote: A hop is one body worth crossing the system for: open the system map, pick it, set the autopilot, wait. Bodies worth less than {n} CR are not counted, because nobody flies to them.
ui.hOreNote: Belt ores are what mining contracts and the daily task ask for. The percentage is the richest showing in the system, and it decides whether filling the hold is one trip or four.
ui.hPtypeNote: Two achievements name a planet type: Almost Like Home wants an Earth-like world, There Could Be Life Here an Ammonia one. Both are also the best-paying scans in the game.
ui.hModuleNote: Nothing in an outfitter is locked behind a faction or a reputation. What a shop carries depends only on the station, and the game never tells you which one you are looking at until you open its menu.
ui.hLandableNote: A landing run is only worth carrying the Planetary Vehicle if a single jump gives you several digs.
ui.nothingInRange: Nothing within {ly} ly of {sys}. Raise the jump range.
ui.viaGate: {n} via warp gate (both ends must be repaired)
ui.isolated: That system sits in an isolated pocket of space with no connection to the rest of the galaxy.
ui.needRange: A jump range of at least {ly} ly is needed to cross generated space.
ui.approxRoute: About {jumps} across {ly} ly of open space.
ui.pMissionMeaning: Missions, stations, engineers and warp gates are only placed in named systems.
ui.pMissionWhy: Everything else in the galaxy is generated, and the game never sends you to one.
ui.pFuelMeaning: The primary star is a class you can scoop from.
ui.pFuelWhy: Routes fail without a scoopable star in range.
ui.pStationWhy: Stations are hand-placed. No station means no trading or outfitting.
ui.pBeltMeaning: At least one asteroid belt, each with exactly 3 ores.
ui.pLandTypes: Rock, Ice, High Metal and Metal Rich. Nothing else can be landed on.
ui.pLandWhy: Surface mining is the only source of some craft materials.
ui.pEngMeaning: An engineer here upgrades certain module types.
ui.pEngCount: 10 postings: 5 engineers, each at a core and a deep-space station.
ui.pGateMeaning: One end of a warp gate.
ui.pGateCost: 1 Zentarks Stone and 30,000,000 CR per end. Both ends must be repaired.
ui.pAuthMeaning: Bodies come from the shipped data, not the generator.
ui.pAuthCount: 112 systems. Everything else is generated from the system's seed.
ui.pSecNote: Security is set on only 97 catalogue systems; the rest default to Anarchy.
ui.pShareCheap: Cheap ore takes the larger share of a belt.
ui.pDeepOre: Never in a belt's scan. Crack asteroids with Seismic charges: in these systems some hold 3–6 tons of it.
ui.pShareCostly: Costly ore takes the smaller share of a belt.
ui.pHuntWhat: One of five expedition types. A StarHunter task names one star class and asks you to find a set number of them.
ui.pHuntOthers: Nebula Exploration, Famous Star Exploration, Planet Hunter, Life Searcher.
ui.pHuntList: The 13 classes a task can name, rarest first, with how many systems hold one.
ui.pHuntWatch: Three classes have no system in reachable space, so those tasks cannot be finished.
ui.byDev: Galaxy Genome is made by SKV Games.
ui.notAffiliated: Not affiliated with or endorsed by the developer. All game data belongs to SKV Games.
